<!-- pr-reviewer: b1303881f938331eeab1ba7adf77ece898ce7852 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Small, contained change (2 files in `camcraft-ui`, no new dependency or feature flag, no snapshot PNGs, no process files, no CHANGELOG edit).
- Platform guards are right: the thread-local, `set_parent` and `parent()` in `crates/ui/src/file_dialog.rs` are all `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, `shell_window.rs` is itself native-only, and `rfd` is a native-only dependency, so wasm32 never sees the new code. (The wasm32 target is not installed on this machine, so I read the guards rather than running `cargo check`.)
- A missing handle falls back to an unowned dialog (`if let Some` / `match ... None => dialog`) with no unwrap/expect/panic. `set_parent` ignores repeat calls, and the `RefCell` borrow is scoped inside `with`, so there is no re-entrancy panic.
- The GPU-refusal dialog stays on the "never silent" path.

**Local results** (trial merge with `upstream/main`, clean, macOS arm64)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --test-threads=1` | 531 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The z-order behaviour is hand-checked on Windows 11 only (as the body says); I could not exercise it here. macOS and Linux (portal/GTK parenting through rfd) compile but are unverified in practice.
- `window.focus_window()` runs on every picker open. That is intended, but it will pull the app forward even if the user switched away between the click and the dialog opening; fine for a modal.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b1303881f938331eeab1ba7adf77ece898ce7852 -->
**Independent review.** Ready for the maintainer to merge (the dialog behaviour itself is hand-test only; not exercised here, the GUI was not launched).

What looks good
- Every picker funnels through `crate::file_dialog::FileDialog` (Open, Model, Save, Save As, Post, per-op folder, setup post options, tool library, theme; `state.rs`, `state_per_op.rs`, `state_setup_post_options.rs`, `state_tool_library.rs`); the only direct `rfd` use left is the GPU-refusal `MessageDialog`, which the PR also owns. No call site is missed.
- Window handle: `file_dialog::set_parent` stores the shell's `Arc<winit::window::Window>` in a thread-local right after `create_window`; `native()` calls `rfd::FileDialog::set_parent` only when one exists. With none (headless tests, before the window, a picker called off the owning thread) the dialog is simply unowned, as before. The code is `cfg(not(wasm32))`; the wasm `imp` stays "treated as cancelled". No Windows-only API; no new dependency (`Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` untouched), no snapshot PNG changes.
- Focus: `focus_window()` is requested once at startup and once each time a picker opens, not per frame.

Local results (trial-merged with main a6bd69d8, clean)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`): 531 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Notes (non-blocking)
- Startup `focus_window()` is a request; some Linux window managers (focus-stealing prevention) and macOS ignore or only flash it. Harmless, but then a terminal launch can still start behind on those platforms.
- The per-picker `focus_window()` raises the owner on every dialog open; that is user-initiated so it is fine, but a picker opened from a background action (none found) would steal focus.
- The thread-local assumes pickers run on the shell thread; a picker from a worker thread falls back to an unowned dialog silently.
- No headless test (a `winit::Window` cannot be built in a unit test); a pure unit test of `set_parent`/`parent` being `None` by default would be cheap if wanted.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
